issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a 'Milkable' interface (with messageOnMilk()), but the solution repository introduces an interface named 'Dairy' that provides messageOnMilk() while leaving Milkable.java empty. This naming/type inconsistency between 'Milkable' (expected by the exercise and template Main) and 'Dairy' (used in the solution and by Seal/Goat) is structural and will confuse students about which interface to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' and remove or populate the empty Milkable.java, or update the problem statement and template to refer to 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'. Ensure Seal and Goat implement the same interface name referenced in the problem/template (messageOnMilk()).

issues.description: The problem statement and the template refer to the milk-related interface as 'Milkable' (interface and usages in problem_statement.md and src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java), but the solution implementation defines and uses an interface named 'Dairy' (Dairy.java and classes implement Dairy). This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual entity (the milkable behavior) creates confusion and will prevent students from mapping the requirement to the provided/expected code (and can cause compilation errors if they follow one name but the other is present).
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface and all its usages to 'Milkable' (or conversely rename problem/template references to 'Dairy') so the same identifier is used in the problem statement, template code, and solution. Ensure the interface file and implementations (Goat, Seal) import/implement the exact same name.
